A: The CT 3D reconstruction (Panel A) reveals bony anomalies, including the cervical-1st rib complex, which is associated with the diagnosis of right-sided arterial thoracic outlet syndrome. B: Panel B, a coronal CT slice in anatomical position, shows the subclavian arteries passing through the narrowed thoracic aperture, consistent with the compression mechanism of arterial thoracic outlet syndrome. C: Panel C demonstrates the bony pathology (cervical-1st rib complex) visualized during dynamic positioning (overhead abduction), supporting the diagnosis of arterial thoracic outlet syndrome. D: Panel D shows the clinical consequence of the bony anomalies and positional compression, specifically the occlusion of the right subclavian artery, which is the key diagnostic finding for arterial thoracic outlet syndrome.
